spec.scope: The project will build a personal notes REST API using Node.js and Express, with operations for creating, listing, and deleting notes. The notes are stored in-memory using a JavaScript Object with sequential integer IDs starting at 1 for new notes. The API does not include authentication or a frontend and operates entirely server-side.

decisions.decision: Store notes in an in-memory JavaScript Object.
decisions.rationale: This fits the requirement for temporary, volatile storage and allows fast data access and modification during requests.

decisions.decision: Generate sequential integer IDs starting at 1 for new notes using a JavaScript function.
decisions.rationale: This ensures each note has a unique and predictable server-assigned identifier without needing user input.

decisions.decision: Serve the API at the root path without a version or /api prefix.
decisions.rationale: This simplifies the URL structure and aligns with the provided design specification.

acceptance_criteria.description: Create a note: POST /notes with JSON body { "title": "<string>", "body": "<string>", "category": "<string>", "tags": ["<string>"] }. The response must include the created note with a server-assigned id.
Return a 400 error if any required field (title, body, category, tags) is missing when creating a note.
List all notes: GET /notes should return an array of notes with fields { "id": "<integer>", "title": "<string>", "body": "<string>", "category": "<string>", "tags": ["<string>"] } for each note.

Delete a note: DELETE /notes/:id should delete the note with the given id and return a 204 status code. If the note does not exist, it should return a 404 status code with an error object { "error": { "message": "Note not found" } }.

files_to_create.purpose: Sets up the Node.js server, mounts all routes, and calls app.listen to accept HTTP requests.
Contains the main Express application setup, route definitions, and in-memory data handling logic.
Provides functionality to generate sequential integer IDs starting at 1 for new notes.

out_of_scope: Any form of data persistence beyond in-memory storage.
